headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: Perplexity can ingest uploaded content and browse externally, while the Awesome-Prompt-Engineering repo is a non-runnable content source with no isolation or trust controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime or I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject B. B can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context, but there is no documented shared channel or automatic feed from A into B. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or user-uploaded content, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies A-derived text into B prompts or uploads A content to B
IF B is configured to treat uploaded text as instructions
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workflows
Do not paste A outputs into B without review
Use a prompt delimiter and instruction/content separation
Disable or avoid uploading untrusted A-derived files to B
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can upload PDFs/images and send browsing context to vendor services, while A is a content repository with no execution or isolation controls. There is no shared filesystem documented, but if A-derived material is placed into B, it can flow to Perplexity's backend. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use through user-mediated transfer.
conditions: IF A-derived documents or notes are uploaded into B
IF B is used on sensitive material that should not leave the vendor backend
mitigations: Avoid uploading sensitive A-derived material to B
Redact secrets before any B query
Use local-only summarization before sending content to B
Review B privacy settings and retention options
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploads to B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is a non-runnable content-writing repository with no write, shell, or network capabilities; B cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shell. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface documented, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF A is replaced with a runnable agent that writes shared state
IF B gains filesystem or git write permissions
mitigations: Keep A as a read-only reference source
Leave B's filesystem and git writes disabled
Separate any future writable agents into distinct workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: B performs multi-hop browsing and can present cited answers, so if A-derived content is used as source material, B may propagate errors or misleading instructions without strong verification. A itself is only a static prompt-engineering resource, but the pair still creates a plausible chain where B treats imported A content as authoritative.
conditions: IF B is prompted to summarize or operationalize A-derived content
IF B is not instructed to verify claims against primary sources
mitigations: Require B to cite primary sources only
Ask B to label uncertainty and unsupported claims
Cross-check B outputs against original sources
Use A only as a reference index, not as authority
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source content repository with no touched personal data classes, while B handles search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context under vendor-hosted processing. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented between them, but if regulated data is uploaded into B, compliance obligations may differ from A's static public content model.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into B
IF the operator expects A's public-content posture to apply to B's vendor-hosted processing
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to B
Check B retention and privacy settings before use
Keep A limited to public, non-sensitive content
Document data-class handling for each workflow
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency/DPA review
